Where should an expanded task’s controls live?

The grouped bottom tray scored 8.50/10. It shows all five values and names the task they belong to. The inline version with a calendar beside the time scored 8.00 and keeps every edit at the task. Try each with the same notes, tags and dates.

Tap the date or time, add or remove a tag, then tap the priority dot four times to cycle None → Low → Mid → High → None. Choose Long tags to see how the placement changes.

Compare the details

390 pt crops. Bottom controls are shown beneath their card here. The review sheets below show their actual distance from the task.

The early inline layouts gave each tag only 60 pt. Words broke midword and pushed the bottom controls down. Giving longer tags a full row reduced the four-tag card from 210 to 150 pt at 390 pt. The calendar cue also shows the day and time together. All three final reviewers still found the borderless priority dot difficult to recognize in the inline version.

The five bottom buttons use the order and right alignment from multi-edit. Their 252 pt stack put several unrelated tasks between the controls and the open card. The grouped tray is 114 pt tall for the sample task, repeats the task title, and spells out the priority beside its icon. It still asks the eye to travel between the card and the bottom of the phone.

The two adjacent dates were easiest to compare in place. The previous strip kept long tag names readable, but the deadline changed rows as other values grew. Layouts were rated as complete alternatives, so the scores do not isolate the effect of moving Project.

Padding around the time

The previous strip put the time 1 pt from the card edge. With the same inline layout and a 12 pt right inset, reviewers scored the 8 pt left inset 9.00, 12 pt 9.50, and 16 pt 8.83. All three gave 12 pt the highest mark. The two follow-up alternatives carry that inset into collapsed rows so the completion circle stays in the same column when the task opens.

Adaptive vertical spacing, trailing relative deadlines and the checked bottom workspace menu are fixed throughout this study.

How the study ran

Nine independent Codex UI reviewers scored orientation, scanability, affordance, legibility and composition in half-point steps from zero to two. Three reviewers scored the reference first (7.50/10). Three fresh reviewers rated four layouts and three insets. Three more reviewed six layouts after the refinements. The 42 ballots are equally weighted within each condition.

The first comparison showed the whole populated screen and crops for empty and long-tag cards. Those crops omitted detached controls. The follow-up shows all three full screens for every layout. Compare means within the same panel. The reference moved from 8.50 to 8.00 between panels.

Native references came from the PR #124 iPhone 18 Pro Max captures at 93e0189. Its picker and bulk-bar SwiftUI sources match rebased main at e8ae94f. The surrounding Planner chrome comes from the previous iPhone capture at 4fe70da. Task layouts and input are browser simulations on a fixed 28-task fixture at standard text size in light appearance. Edits update a single task in memory. Device touch, keyboard behavior, VoiceOver and native motion were outside this review.
